items.title: Welcome by the School Board President, Mike Wells

publicComments.name: Meng Zhao
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expanding the Orion Mandarin Immersion program to accommodate all interested applicants in the first round of the lottery, presenting data on growing demand, wait lists, and academic benefits of Mandarin immersion education.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strobe
publicComments.summary: Advocated for expanding the Orion Mandarin Immersion program, presenting data showing socioeconomically disadvantaged students in MI schools consistently outperform their peers, and requesting the board add an additional TK/K classroom and consider a supplemental application.

publicComments.name: Kimberly Abbey
publicComments.summary: Shared her personal experience as a TK parent in the MI program, praising its tight-knit community and the gift of Mandarin language for her son, and hoping more families can join.

publicComments.name: Weiji
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about limited kindergarten spots in the MI program as an immigrant Chinese family who moved to Redwood City specifically for the program, and asked the board to expand it.

publicComments.name: Christina Lee
publicComments.summary: Described being stuck at number one on the MI wait list for over a year while investing in private Mandarin after-school programs, and advocated for expanding the MI program so all interested families can access it.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade MI student shared her personal journey from struggling academically in first grade to placing 17th in a national math competition, crediting Mandarin immersion, and urged the board to support all students who need this opportunity.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Yielded time to Meng Zhao to present additional data on growth projections for Orion showing a declining trend line they believe is inaccurate, and reiterated the request to accommodate first-round applicants and consider a supplemental application.

publicComments.name: Chris Lau
publicComments.summary: Shared that he and his wife moved to Redwood City partly because of the MI program and hopes to enroll his daughter in the future, thanking the board for considering expanding it.

publicComments.name: Katherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Shared her experience as a parent whose child went through Mandarin Immersion and then Northstar, noting both programs have extensive wait lists and strong academic results, and suggested these programs merit additional resources and expanded capacity.

publicComments.name: Xingxing
publicComments.summary: Shared as a first-generation immigrant from China (with a Ukrainian immigrant husband) that they moved to Redwood City in 2019 and hope to enroll their two children in the Mandarin Immersion program for heritage language access.

publicComments.name: James Harbold
publicComments.summary: Supported the Mandarin Immersion program as a parent whose daughter is applying, noting his wife is from China and he studied Mandarin in Hong Kong, and asked the district to help families like his gain access to the program.
